title: K-Pg Extinction: Asteroid Impact & Global Catastrophe

scenes.title: The Great Extinction Trigger
scenes.narration: Around 66 million years ago, a catastrophic event plunged Earth into a devastating crisis, leading to the Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) mass extinction and wiping out 75% of life.

scenes.title: The Chicxulub Impact
scenes.narration: The primary cause was a massive 10-15 km wide Chicxulub asteroid striking the Yucatán Peninsula, creating a 180 km wide crater and releasing energy equivalent to billions of atomic bombs.

scenes.title: Immediate Devastation
scenes.narration: The impact generated massive shockwaves, superheated ejecta, and colossal tsunamis up to 100 meters high, causing immediate regional destruction and igniting widespread wildfires across continents.

scenes.title: Atmospheric Blockage
scenes.narration: Vast quantities of dust, soot, and sulfur aerosols were ejected into the atmosphere, forming a dense, global cloud layer that effectively blocked sunlight from reaching Earth's surface for months to years.

scenes.title: Impact Winter & Photosynthesis Collapse
scenes.narration: The prolonged darkness led to a global impact winter, causing temperatures to plummet and halting photosynthesis. This collapsed the base of the food web, starving both herbivores and carnivores across ecosystems.

scenes.title: Global vs. Local Effects
scenes.narration: While the initial impact caused immense local devastation (tsunamis, shockwaves), the more widespread and prolonged damage came from the global climate disruption, particularly the impact winter, affecting all ecosystems.

scenes.title: Ocean Acidification
scenes.narration: The impact also released vast amounts of sulfur into the atmosphere, forming sulfuric acid that precipitated as acid rain. This led to widespread ocean acidification, dissolving shells and skeletons of marine organisms, devastating marine food webs.

scenes.title: Volcanism vs. Impact
scenes.narration: While massive volcanic activity (Deccan Traps) occurred concurrently, its gradual effects differed from the asteroid's sudden, catastrophic impact. The impact delivered a rapid, devastating blow that overwhelmed ecosystems immediately.

scenes.title: Dinosaur Extinction
scenes.narration: Large, non-avian dinosaurs, especially herbivores, struggled immensely due to the collapse of plant life. Their size and metabolic needs made them particularly vulnerable to the rapid and severe environmental changes.

scenes.title: Mammalian Rise
scenes.narration: Small, often burrowing mammals, birds, and some reptiles, with lower metabolic rates and diverse diets, were better equipped to survive the harsh conditions. This paved the way for the Cenozoic Era and mammalian diversification.

scenes.title: Survival Niches
scenes.narration: Species in aquatic environments, those with dormancy capabilities, or those relying on detritus rather than photosynthesis, had a higher chance of survival. These niches offered refuge from the immediate and prolonged surface devastation.

scenes.title: The Multi-faceted Catastrophe
scenes.narration: The K-Pg extinction was not a single event but a cascade of interconnected environmental disasters: impact, wildfires, tsunamis, impact winter, and ocean acidification, creating a perfect storm for life on Earth.

scenes.title: Geological Evidence
scenes.narration: The iridium anomaly, shocked quartz, and microtektites found globally at the K-Pg boundary layer provide compelling geological evidence for a massive extraterrestrial impact, corroborating the Chicxulub event.

scenes.title: Future Impact Preparedness
scenes.narration: Understanding the K-Pg event informs our strategies for planetary defense. Detecting and potentially deflecting future asteroid threats is crucial, as even smaller impacts could cause significant regional or global devastation.
